Last Call for Des Moines Farmers Market: Your Essential September Shopping & Cooking Guide

As autumn approaches in Central Iowa, the beloved Downtown Farmers' Market in Des Moines enters its final weeks, offering a bountiful harvest of late-summer and fall produce. This comprehensive guide will help you make the most of September's market offerings in the Historic Court Avenue District.

What's in Season at the Des Moines Farmers Market

September brings peak harvest season to Central Iowa farms, with vendors offering:

  • Sweet corn from Grimes and Ankeny farms
  • Heirloom tomatoes from Valley Junction growers
  • Fall squash varieties from Warren County
  • Fresh apples from local orchards near Waukee
  • Local honey from Des Moines area beekeepers

Shopping Tips for September Market Days

Best Times to Visit

The Downtown Farmers' Market runs every Saturday from 7 am to noon. For the best selection, arrive before 9 am when Court Avenue is bustling with early-bird shoppers from across the Greater Des Moines metro.

Parking & Transportation

Take advantage of free parking at the Science Center of Iowa or hop on the D-Line Downtown Shuttle from the East Village. DART buses also offer convenient Saturday morning routes to the market.

Local Chef Recommendations

We spoke with chefs from popular Des Moines restaurants like Django and Alba about their favorite September market finds:

  • Roasted butternut squash soup with locally sourced ingredients
  • Fresh apple cider from Iowa orchards
  • Late-season tomato gazpacho
  • Farm-fresh egg frittatas with market vegetables

Beyond Produce: Market Vendors to Visit

Don't miss these local favorites:

  • La Mie Bakery's fresh pastries
  • Maytag Dairy Farms' blue cheese
  • The Corn Stand's roasted sweet corn
  • Local food trucks along 3rd Street

Supporting Local Agriculture

Shopping at the Downtown Farmers' Market supports over 300 local vendors from 50 Iowa counties, helping preserve Iowa's rich agricultural heritage.
